title: Gurunam Singh v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Manoj Kumar Gupta, J.; Manish Kumar Nigam, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; Clause 6.5 objection directed; recovery stayed four weeks.
headnote: A writ challenging a recovery citation for electricity dues was disposed of on the licensee's statement that the consumer has a Clause 6.5 objection remedy, to be decided before recovery. Two weeks to object; two weeks for respondent no.2 to decide; recovery in abeyance four weeks, then to abide that decision. If no objection is filed in time, the order lapses.
facts: The petitioner, Gurunam Singh, filed a writ petition challenging a recovery citation dated 25 April 2023 issued by respondent no.4 for recovery of electricity dues from him. Counsel for U.P. Power Corporation Limited submitted that the petitioner had a remedy of filing an objection under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and that any objection so filed would be decided before recovering the amount under the citation. The Court did not examine the underlying dues.

holding_units.holding: A consumer challenging a recovery citation for electricity dues has the remedy of filing an objection under Clause 6.5. The writ was disposed of with two weeks to file the objection, to be decided by respondent no.2 within the next two weeks; recovery remains in abeyance for four weeks and thereafter abides that decision. If no objection is filed within time, the order lapses and the licensee may proceed in accordance with law.

not_decided.point: Validity of the recovery citation dated 25.04.2023 and the electricity dues claimed
not_decided.note: Left to decision on the petitioner's Clause 6.5 objection by respondent no.2.
